No tracked file (outside this manifest's four pathspec exclusions) references the operator's numeric uid in the phrase spelling -- the three-letter id-word immediately followed by the token. The token is computed from the running process (id -u) and never written here: a detector that must state the identifier it hunts publishes that identifier in the tracked file that exists to keep it out -- the same asymmetry as its bare-token sibling and the computed classes in scripts/statement_lint.py. Until 2026-08-19 the pattern was anchored with the word-boundary escape under git grep -E, whose ERE engine does not implement that escape: the predicate matched zero lines by construction and could not fail. Corrected to -P and measured at correction time on the tracked tree: zero lines on the surface -- the underlying fact is true, so this claim stays GREEN and, unlike its sibling, declares no exposure. The phrase's occurrences outside the surface (5 lines in 2 files under docs/adrs/ at correction time) sit in the locus the claim's own pathspecs exclude by design.

Until 2026-08-19 the pattern was anchored with the word-boundary escape under git grep -E, whose ERE engine does not implement that escape: the predicate matched zero lines by construction and could not fail. Corrected to -P and measured at correction time on the tracked tree: RED, 212 lines across 41 files -- 211 lines in 40 files under runs/THR-SUBAGENT/, 1 line in 1 file under .verity/evidence/. Declared RED as observed, the same discipline the falsifier register applies to a known red (the bypass_ft_bash_unbound and FT-28 rows): this claim is expected to stay RED until the operator records a decision on the exposure it now measures, and a GREEN here means the exposure left the tracked surface. It is declared and not repaired because the repair is not this claim's to take: three of the carrying files are cited by sha256 from tracked conformance records that resolve today, and the order of redaction and re-pinning is an operator decision.

ADR-020 D3: every emitted in-toto Statement conforms to D2's allowlist. Unlike the privacy-lint claims above, this one presides over the EMITTED ARTIFACT and not over the tree -- side-car Statements are written beside the receipt under an ignored directory, so no git grep can ever reach them, which is the defect ADR-020 D1 measured in privacy-lint-user-paths. The --selftest arm is the control: it requires the boundary to accept a conforming specimen and refuse five leaking ones on every run, so the claim still discriminates on a checkout where no run has emitted anything yet. tests/bypass_att_prose_leak_fixture.sh drives the same detector with more arms.
